learning: If s-bend and slalom losses stay at 0 and max_error stays near 0.061 m, the controller is responding too late at the edge, not losing the tape. If oval oscillation stays at or below 0.3 with progress near 0.7, the footprint is working and the next step is gain tuning (kp) for the edge drift. If oval oscillation rises above 0.33 or oval progress falls below 0.5, the larger footprint is blurring the centroid, so revert to 0.012 m.
notes: Iteration 5 controller kept unchanged, so the race isolates the Builder's sensor_size change from 0.012 m to 0.016 m at the 12 cm span. Keep the iteration 5 gains.
rationale: Iteration 5 is the best race so far (151.91). The ±0.06 m outer span removed line losses on s-bend and slalom (0.0 per run, down from 0.9 to 1.0), and oval finished 1 of 20 trials with progress 0.71. The remaining failure is that every s-bend and slalom trial still ends off track at max_error about 0.061 m, so the robot drifts to the edge while still reading the tape. Oval steering oscillation is 0.327, just above the 0.3 target. The Builder's single change is sensor_size from 0.012 m to 0.016 m, with the span, y, wheel_track and body unchanged. I keep the iteration 5 controller exactly (kp 1.0, kd 0.2, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.0, last_direction, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]). Changing gains at the same time as the footprint would make it impossible to attribute the result. Base speed is not the constraint: the oval finish took 1.94 s, under the 3 s limit. Larger footprints overlap more, so the centroid should change more smoothly as the tape edge crosses each sensor. That may reduce the edge drift and the oval jitter, but it may also blur the centroid on gentle bends. The expected result is that s-bend and slalom max_error stays below 0.06 m or runs progress further, with oval oscillation at or below 0.3 and oval progress near 0.7. The main risk is that oval progress falls, which the Builder's fallback rule covers.
